newsitem.title: USA: UOL sees turning profitable in 1997.
newsitem.headline: UOL sees turning profitable in 1997.

text.p: UOL Publishing Inc is comfortable with forecasts that it will make a profit in 1997 for the first time in two years, company executives said.

According to First Call's consensus estimate, UOL is expected to earn $0.38 per share in fiscal 1997. The McLean, Virginia-based company reported a loss per share of $0.34 for the first quarter of 1997, and lost $3.88 per share in 1996.
"As of today, management feels comfortable with those estimates," said Lenn Kurtzman, chief financial officer at UOL said in an interview. "Our business plan is on target."
UOL has recently begun selling an Internet-based educational database that it calls an "electronic campus," a product it has spent more than two years moving on to the Internet.
In 1984, the company started out publishing adult education courses on CD-ROMs.
UOL chairman and chief executive Narasimham Kannan said the company began experimenting with the Internet in 1991, as it began to see cyberspace as an emerging market for electronic communication.
In the last couple of years, the company adapted its electronic coursework to the World Wide Web, and began selling it to clients this year.
"Its the World Wide Web that really caused this sea change in our business model," he said.
UOL continues to expect to meet a goal of 75 clients by year end. Each client is expected to generate up to $200,000 in annual revenues for the company.
It says it has 20 new clients so far this year, including AT&T Corp and Digital Equipment Corp, as well as Georgetown University and University of California at Berkeley.
